entry_points.text: Flush resets state and image; return ensures registers present; idle drops tile ownership when active.
Control queries support and permissions, acquiring only on 64-bit. Status reports vector idle capped with never-used sentinel. Tracer forwards updates.

exports.text: Clone builds an off-hardware context needing reload, inheriting under protection with thread limits, clearing accelerators and syncing shadow stacks. Faults map to arithmetic signals or spurious zero; supervisor restores first; context follows the task aligned.

Debug sets need their extension enabled. Shadow stack gives one aligned pointer with sync and invalidation. Extended transfers require whole buffers with control checks and presence updates. Layouts overlap with a feature header and separate supervisor part.
Legacy 32-bit state translates control, tags, pointers and slots between compact and extended forms; debugger picks emulation, legacy or extended sources.

Signal save uses legacy and extended buffers with size and key; restore clears on failure. Alloc reserves aligned space; helpers locate, copy and clear features. No hardware gives soft emulation; faults retry; disabled gives null.

Resume restores user, supervisor and dynamic controls when supported. Key updates need support and valid numbers or fail. Independent save and restore need compacted support and valid masks or warn idly.

Disable checks allow on equality, forbid current matches, limit shared images to restores, else strip handled bits and forbid leftovers. Enabling forwards faults; restricted denies; group masks readable; trampolines use dedicated memory.

hazards.text: User legacy access allows faults with hardening and safe failure; kernel access traps errors via tables; width picks 32 or 64-bit.
Verify faults are memory errors, mismatches invalid with warnings; call changes unsupported. Call decode needs call opcode or warns null.

invariants.text: Copy offset and size derive from task layout and default size. Debugger sync targets only the current task; external updates drop hardware linkage first.
Tags compress to empty-or-valid bytes one way and rebuild empty, zero, valid or special from occupancy and encoding the other; codes run zero through three.

Frames validate by markers and sizes, else legacy fallback with base features. Software bytes track sizes and sets; user areas hold a presence bitmap. Saves narrow dynamically, mark base present and propagate keys when supported.

Restore picks format by capability and fills gaps from the initial image. Masks limit to enabled features with separate supervisor handling. Compat preserves supervisor, folds legacy and enforces control strictly on 64-bit, masked on 32-bit.
Per-feature tables hold offsets, sizes, flags and order; all-ones means uninitialized. Bits mark supervisor and alignment. Independent ops need valid masks or warn; order follows offsets.
Permission merge sizes areas, checks stacks, then publishes ordered masks. Dumps omit notes without features, else write a typed header with per-component descriptors.
Idle is a five-byte nop; activation emits jump or call. Patching verifies then queues or writes at once. Updates repatch calls; trampolines are protected, created once and refreshed under lock.

locks.text: Register work runs under the floating point lock. Drop also blocks preemption. Lock-and-load warns in unsafe interrupt or kernel-thread use.
User access holds the loaded lock with faults disabled; faults unlock to resolve then retry. Masks limit features; supervisor handled separately. Partial updates and fatal errors possible.

Size gives maximum frames; stack checks under signal lock fail when small. Permission checks guard speculation, fast-accept covered, else lock and expand; tile mask tabled. Tracer prep holds text lock deferred.

state_machines.text: A flag tracks whether hardware holds current registers; initial reloads, activation and checks move between loaded and need-load.
Saving flows from setup through load and hardware save to legacy and software finish, clearing and retrying on faults.
Boot enables dynamic sizing only with dynamic initial bits; heap frees only when separate. Tracer validates then enqueues. Trampolines clone templates, relocate, wire under lock and harden.

structs.text: Media mask starts all-set and locks after init. Internal and legacy headers each guard inclusion once.
Metadata parallels names, CPU needs, offsets, sizes, flags and order by feature; frames align to 64 bytes.
Copy selects legacy, save or compacted source. Save and restore cover standard, optimized, compacted and supervisor forms.
Return levels are debug one, fault two, double-fault three, with per-CPU entry pointer. Tracer overlays opcodes with offsets; sizes vary by mitigations; logs prefix module.
